before.title: Joint regularity of radial vector and scalar potentials on star-shaped domains
before.statement: Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and star-shaped with centre $a$, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval, let $k\ge1$, and let $B:U\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be of class $C^k$ jointly with $\operatorname{div}B(\cdot,t)=0$ for every $t$. Then the radial witness $A(x,t):=\int_0^1s\,B(a+s(x-a),t)\times(x-a)\,ds$ is $C^k$ jointly on $U\times I$ and $\operatorname{curl}A(\cdot,t)=B(\cdot,t)$ for every $t$. If in addition $C:U\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ is $C^k$ jointly with $\operatorname{curl}C(\cdot,t)=0$ for every $t$, then the radial scalar witness $\phi(x,t):=\int_0^1\langle C(a+s(x-a),t),x-a\rangle\,ds$ is $C^k$ jointly on $U\times I$ and $\nabla\phi(\cdot,t)=-C(\cdot,t)$ for every $t$. For $C^\infty$ data both potentials are $C^\infty$ jointly. No global potential on an arbitrary open set is claimed.
before.strategy: Repeat the compact-rectangle parameter-differentiation argument for every derivative through order $k$; the parameter derivatives are continuous on the compact rectangle $[0,1]\times$-slices, so the radial witness is $C^k$ jointly. The scalar clause applies the published Poincaré lemma and its radial witness. On a ball the construction is local even when $U$ has holes; first and second cohomological obstructions must not be conflated.

references.title: J. Feldman, A. Rechnitzer, E. Yeager, CLP-4 Vector Calculus (UBC), §4.1 (Theorems 4.1.4-4.1.16)
J. Lebl, Basic Analysis II, §9.1 (Leibniz integral rule), Theorem 9.1.1

after.title: Joint regularity of radial vector and scalar potentials on star-shaped domains
after.statement: Regularity convention for a possibly non-open parameter interval I: a map on $U\times I$ is jointly $C^k$ when it is the restriction of a $C^k$ map on some open neighbourhood $N\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ of $U\times I$; jointly $C^\infty$ means the restriction of one smooth map on such an open neighbourhood. For open I these are exactly the usual open-domain classes of def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms. At included endpoints of a nondegenerate time interval, time derivatives are the corresponding relative one-sided derivatives. For empty or singleton I the restriction convention still asserts extension existence and the stated spatial identities, but it does not determine time jets uniquely from the restricted values alone. This convention does not require a fixed uniform enlargement of an unbounded I. Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and star-shaped with centre $a$, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval, let $k\ge1$, and let $B:U\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be of class $C^k$ jointly with $\operatorname{div}B(\cdot,t)=0$ for every $t$. Then the radial witness $A(x,t):=\int_0^1s\,B(a+s(x-a),t)\times(x-a)\,ds$ is $C^k$ jointly on $U\times I$ and $\operatorname{curl}A(\cdot,t)=B(\cdot,t)$ for every $t$. If in addition $C:U\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ is $C^k$ jointly with $\operatorname{curl}C(\cdot,t)=0$ for every $t$, then the radial scalar witness $\phi(x,t):=-\int_0^1\langle C(a+s(x-a),t),x-a\rangle\,ds$ is $C^k$ jointly on $U\times I$ and $\nabla\phi(\cdot,t)=-C(\cdot,t)$ for every $t$. For $C^\infty$ data both potentials are $C^\infty$ jointly. No global potential on an arbitrary open set is claimed.
after.strategy:
The interval regularity convention is supplied explicitly in the statement, rather than treating the imported open-domain definition as already covering non-open products. To prove regularity in that same extension sense, choose an open-neighbourhood Ck extension of the data (intersect the extensions' neighbourhoods if both B and C are used). Let P be the set of (x,t) for which every (a+s(x-a),t), 0<=s<=1, lies in that open extension domain. It contains UxI by star-shapedness. It is open: at any one point of P its compact radial segment has a finite cover by balls contained in the extension domain; equivalently its distance from the closed complement is positive, and continuity of the radial map uniformly in s keeps all nearby (x,t) segments inside those balls. The identical radial integral of the extension data is therefore defined on P and is Ck there by the compact parameter proof below; its restriction is the stated potential. For smooth input use its one smooth extension and the same argument through every finite order. Curl-freeness/divergence-freeness is only needed on the original slices to establish the field identities there, not on the enlarged neighbourhood. Set w=x-a and z_s=a+sw. The spatial star-shaped hypothesis puts z_s in U for 0<=s<=1. For any compact spatial box Q contained in U and compact parameter subinterval J contained in I, the radial image of [0,1]xQ is compact inside U. Each component of the vector and scalar radial integrands is a finite sum of products of the polynomial factors s,w and the Ck components of B(z_s,t) or C(z_s,t). Chain and product rules give every mixed spatial/time word derivative through total order k as a continuous function of (s,x,t) on the corresponding compact product. Apply thm-differentiation-under-the-integral-sign-on-a-compact-rectangle in each parameter coordinate, with others fixed, and induct on derivative order. Uniform continuity on the compact product and lem-uniform-integral-error-bound show that each resulting derivative integral is jointly continuous. Included endpoints of nondegenerate time intervals use the relative endpoint derivatives of the compact-rectangle supplier. For empty or singleton I, construct the potentials using a chosen ambient extension on its open radial-admissibility set and restrict; this proves the same extension existence and spatial identities, without claiming uniquely determined time jets on the degenerate restriction. Thus both explicit integrals are jointly Ck, without assuming k+1 derivatives, and applying this for every k gives the smooth assertion. No surface-measure or Lebesgue integration/Choice branch of lem-em-parameter-integrals is needed: these are ordinary one-dimensional integrals in s on [0,1].

At each fixed t, the positive vector integral is exactly the witness of thm-a-divergence-free-c1-field-on-a-star-shaped-open-set-has-a-vector-potential, so curl A=B. For the scalar branch put Psi_C(x,t)=integral_0^1 <C(z_s,t),w> ds, and take phi_C=-Psi_C. The published Poincare theorem gives grad Psi_C=C; its convention is positive gradient, so it cannot itself justify grad of the positive integral being -C. Explicitly, curl C=0 means partial_j C_i=partial_i C_j in three dimensions. Differentiation gives partial_j Psi_C=integral_0^1 [C_j(z_s,t)+s sum_i w_i partial_j C_i(z_s,t)] ds. Replace partial_j C_i by partial_i C_j; the integrand becomes d/ds[s C_j(z_s,t)]. thm-newton-leibniz-with-interior-derivative gives C_j(x,t)-0*C_j(a,t)=C_j(x,t), hence partial_j phi_C=-C_j. Therefore grad phi_C=-C with the stated finite-k and smooth joint regularity. In particular for C=e1, phi_C=-(x1-a1), so grad phi_C=-e1; the old positive integral gave +e1 and was a concrete contradiction. Neither a general non-star-shaped global existence claim nor a new physical assumption is introduced. On a ball the same construction is local even when the surrounding open set has holes; scalar circulation and vector-flux obstructions remain distinct.

references.title: J. Feldman, A. Rechnitzer, E. Yeager, CLP-4 Vector Calculus (UBC), §4.1 (Theorems 4.1.4-4.1.16)
J. Lebl, Basic Analysis II, §9.1 (Leibniz integral rule), Theorem 9.1.1

before.title: Smooth scalar and vector potentials on a star-shaped space-time region
before.reference: core-conditional-proofs.md#K7 and mathematical-prerequisites.md#M05; interfaces aligned to lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials and def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions
before.design_state: complete-exact-conditional-research-argument; local second application of the published joint-regularity supplier; not an independent acceptance
before.statement: Let $c>0$. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be an open set that is star-shaped with respect to a point $a\in\Omega$ ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]) and let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with at least two elements ([[def-interval]]). Fix an integer $k\ge2$ and let $E,B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be fields of class $C^k$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-em-fields]]) satisfying the two source-free Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on $\Omega\times I$ in their pointwise form $$\operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,$$ with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative $\partial_t$ at fixed position of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. Then there are a scalar potential $\varphi:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{k-1}$ jointly and a vector potential $A:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^k$ jointly ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]) with $$B=\operatorname{curl}A,\qquad E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA\qquad\text{on }\Omega\times I.$$ If $E$ and $B$ are of class $C^\infty$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$, then $\varphi$ and $A$ may be chosen of class $C^\infty$ jointly. Conversely, if $\varphi$ and $A$ are of class $C^\infty$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ and $E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B:=\operatorname{curl}A$ are their field pair, then $(E,B)$ satisfies $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ on $\Omega\times I$. The theorem asserts existence on the stated star-shaped domain only: it claims no global potential on a general open $\Omega$, no boundary or decay condition on the potentials, and no uniqueness; potentials are auxiliary objects of the framework and not claimed to be observable.

references.title: L. D. Landau and E. M. Lifshitz, The Classical Theory of Fields, Third Revised English Edition (Course of Theoretical Physics vol. 2, Pergamon Press 1971, 387 pp.)
references.locator: §16 printed pp. 44-45 (the four-potential A_k and its relation to the scalar and vector potentials) and §17 printed pp. 46-48, equations (17.3)-(17.4): E = -grad phi - (1/c) dA/dt and H = curl A

references.title: David Tong, Electromagnetism, University of Cambridge Part II Mathematical Tripos lecture notes (2026 printing, 236 pp.)
references.locator: §5.3.1 printed pp. 105-106: the potential representation E = -grad phi - dA/dt, B = curl A as the general solution of the two source-free Maxwell equations

references.title: David J. Griffiths, Introduction to Electrodynamics, 3rd edition (Prentice Hall 1999, 596 pp.; full scanned text)
references.locator: §10.1.1 printed pp. 416-418: the potential formulation and the two inhomogeneous equations for V and A on which the potential representation rests

before.physical_scope: The fields and potentials of the classical vacuum electromagnetic framework of [[def-em-fields]], [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] and [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]] on a single inertial laboratory region over a star-shaped spatial region. The only physical hypothesis used is the pair of source-free Maxwell equations (absence of magnetic charge and Faraday's law) as adopted in the postulate; no source equation, no regularity beyond the stated joint class, and no assertion that the potentials are observable are included. The star-shaped hypothesis is a genuine restriction on the spatial region, and the companion examples exhibit a divergence-free field on a non-star-shaped region with no global vector potential.

before.title: Gauge reachability: Lorenz gauge on the all-space slab and Coulomb gauge on a bounded smooth domain, with residual freedom
before.reference: core-conditional-proofs.md#K7 and completed-expansion-arguments.md#W6; bounded-domain branch closed locally with the published elliptic resolvent and higher-order Dirichlet estimates
before.design_state: complete branch argument for the two declared branches; the older global gauge promise on bounded domains with prescribed data is outside the statement, as the design requires
before.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ in branch (a) and the Axiom of Choice together with $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as declared by its weak-solvability lemmas in branch (b) ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $c>0$ and let $(\varphi,A)$ be a potential pair of the framework ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-em-fields]]) with field pair $(E,B)$ and Lorenz divergence $G=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi$. (a) [All-space slab; Lorenz gauge] Let $t_0<T$ and let $(\varphi,A)$ be of class $C^\infty$ in the extension sense on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ (the restriction of a $C^\infty$ pair on $\mathbb R^3\times J$ for some open interval $J\supset[t_0,T]$; [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Then there is a gauge function $\chi$ of class $C^\infty$ in the extension sense on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ with $\chi(\cdot,t_0)=0$, $\partial_t\chi(\cdot,t_0)=0$ and $W\chi=G$ on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$; the transformed pair $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$, has the same field pair $(E,B)$, and any two such gauge functions differ by a solution of $W\chi=0$. This is the exact content of [[lem-em-gauge-wave-reachability]] read for potential pairs of the framework; its physical content is that every smooth potential representation of a field pair on a slab admits a Lorenz-gauge representative with zero gauge Cauchy data at $t_0$, without changing the fields. (b) [Bounded smooth domain; Coulomb gauge] Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]), let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval and let $(\varphi,A)$ be of class $C^\infty$ on a neighbourhood of $\bar\Omega\times\bar I$. Fix a smooth time-independent Dirichlet datum $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$. Then there is a gauge function $\psi$, of class $C^\infty$ on a neighbourhood of $\bar\Omega\times\bar I$, with $\psi(\cdot,t)|_{\partial\Omega}=g$ for every $t\in I$, such that $$\operatorname{div}(A+\nabla\psi)(\cdot,t)=0\qquad\text{on }\Omega\text{ for every }t\in I;$$ the transformed pair $T_\psi(\varphi,A)$ is in Coulomb gauge on $\Omega\times I$ and has the same field pair $(E,B)$ ([[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]). The generator is unique among such generators with datum $g$; if $g=0$, then $\psi$ is the unique generator with zero boundary values. (c) [Residual freedom on star-shaped domains] Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and star-shaped ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]) and let $(\varphi,A)$, $(\tilde\varphi,\tilde A)$ be two potential pairs of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-interval]]) with the same field pair, both in Lorenz gauge. Then there is a gauge function $\chi$ of class $C^2$ jointly with $(\tilde\varphi,\tilde A)=T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ and $W\chi=0$ on $\Omega\times I$. (d) [Scope] Nothing is asserted about gauge functions meeting arbitrary prescribed boundary or initial restrictions: in (a) the gauge function has zero Cauchy data at $t_0$ and no spatial boundary condition or decay, and $\Omega$ is all of $\mathbb R^3$; in (b) the datum is the fixed time-independent Dirichlet datum $g$ and the Neumann variant with its own compatibility condition for every $t$ is not claimed; the older promise of a global Lorenz gauge on a bounded domain with prescribed boundary data is explicitly outside this result. The Coulomb-gauge statement concerns the spatial divergence in the chosen inertial chart, and the instantaneous appearance of the Coulomb potential is a property of the representation, not a signal: only the field pair $(E,B)$ is physical content ([[def-em-fields]]).
before.strategy:
(a) is [[lem-em-gauge-wave-reachability]] with its hypotheses and countable choice carried verbatim; the pair of the framework enters only through the vocabulary, so nothing is reproved. (b) Fix $g$ and let $h\in C^\infty( ar\Omega)$ be the solution of $-\varepsilon_0\Delta h=0$ in $\Omega$ with $h|_{\partial\Omega}=g$ ([[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]](a) with $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0 I$ and $ho=0$). Let $R$ be the zero-trace Dirichlet solution operator of $-\Delta$: for $F\in L^2(\Omega)$, $R(F)\in H_0^1\cap H^2$ is the unique weak solution of $-\Delta R(F)=F/\varepsilon_0$, equivalently $-\varepsilon_0\Delta R(F)=F$. Existence and uniqueness are [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]](a) with datum $0$ and source $ho=F$; the $L^2$ bound $\|R(F)\|_{L^2}\le(2L)^2\varepsilon_0^{-1}\|F\|_{L^2}$ follows by testing with $R(F)$ and using the squared Poincare bound of [[lem-em-zero-boundary-coercivity]] (constant $(2L)^2$, nonsquared consequence $\|v\|_2\le2L\|
abla v\|_2$), and $R$ maps $H^k(\Omega)$ boundedly into $H^{k+2}(\Omega)$ with constant $C_k$ depending only on $k,\Omega$ by [[thm-higher-order-boundary-regularity-for-dirichlet-problems]] applied to $L=-\Delta$ on the bounded $C^\infty$ domain. Define $F_t:=\varepsilon_0\operatorname{div}A(\cdot,t)\in C^\infty( ar\Omega)$ and $\psi(\cdot,t):=h+R(F_t)$. Then $-\varepsilon_0\Delta\psi(\cdot,t)=\varepsilon_0\operatorname{div}A(\cdot,t)$, so $\operatorname{div}(A+
abla\psi)(\cdot,t)=0$, and $\psi(\cdot,t)|_{\partial\Omega}=g$, for every $t$. Joint smoothness: by linearity of $R$ the difference quotient of $\psi$ in $t$ is $R$ of the difference quotient of $F_t$; since $t\mapsto F_t$ is $C^\infty$ as a map into each $H^k$ (all mixed derivatives of $A$ are jointly continuous and $ ar\Omega	imes ar I$ is compact) and $R$ is bounded $H^k	o H^{k+2}$ and $L^2	o L^2$, induction gives $\partial_t^j\psi(\cdot,t)=R(\partial_t^jF_t)$ for every $j$, a continuous map into every $H^m$, hence into every Sobolev space whose embedding into $C^\ell( ar\Omega)$ is supplied by [[thm-higher-order-sobolev-embedding]] (the bounded $C^\infty$ domain is a bounded extension domain); every mixed derivative $\partial_x^\alpha\partial_t^j\psi=\partial_x^\alpha R(\partial_t^jF_t)$ is therefore jointly continuous on $ ar\Omega	imes ar I$, so $\psi$ is $C^\infty$ in the extension sense and its transform is defined. The field pair is unchanged by [[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]] and the condition $\operatorname{div}(A+
abla\psi)=0$ is Coulomb gauge in the chosen chart. Uniqueness: two generators with the same datum $g$ have a difference that is harmonic on $\Omega$ with zero Dirichlet trace, hence zero, by the uniqueness clause of [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]](a) with $ho=0$. (c) Put $\delta\varphi:=	ilde\varphi-\varphi$, $\delta A:=	ilde A-A$. Then $\operatorname{curl}\delta A=0$ and $-
abla\delta\varphi-\partial_t\delta A=0$; since $\delta A$ is jointly $C^2$ with $\operatorname{curl}\delta A(\cdot,t)=0$ for every $t$, the scalar clause of [[lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials]] gives $\chi_0\in C^2$ jointly with $\delta A=
abla\chi_0$. Then $
abla(\delta\varphi+\partial_t\chi_0)=
abla\delta\varphi+\partial_t
abla\chi_0=
abla\delta\varphi+\partial_t\delta A=0$ (mixed partials of the $C^2$ function $\chi_0$, [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]), and $\Omega$ is star-shaped hence connected, so $\delta\varphi+\partial_t\chi_0=h(t)$ for a $C^1$ function $h$ of $t$ alone. Choose $\eta\in C^2(I)$ with $\eta'=-h$ and set $\chi:=\chi_0+\eta$; then $T_\chi(\varphi,A)=(\varphi-\partial_t\chi_0+h,\ A+
abla\chi_0)=(	ilde\varphi,	ilde A)$. Finally $G(	ilde\varphi,	ilde A)=G(\varphi,A)-W\chi$ by [[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]](b), and both $G$-values vanish, so $W\chi=0$. The linearity of $
abla$ and $\partial_t$ used throughout is [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]; $H^m$ notation is [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], and the elliptic problems use the domains of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]. The declared Choice assumptions enter only through the elliptic existence theorem and the wave supplier and are carried in the statement. No claim beyond (a)-(c) is made.

before.physical_scope: Gauge reachability for potential representations of the classical vacuum electromagnetic framework, in exactly two declared branches: the all-space smooth slab branch, where a Lorenz-gauge representative with zero gauge Cauchy data exists (carrying countable choice through the wave supplier), and the bounded smooth-domain branch, where a Coulomb-gauge representative with a prescribed time-independent smooth Dirichlet datum exists and is unique (carrying the choice assumptions declared by the elliptic supplier). The item also classifies residual freedom on star-shaped domains. It makes no empirical claim, asserts nothing about arbitrary prescribed boundary or initial restrictions, and does not claim that gauge conditions are physically observable.

Then there is a gauge function $\chi$ of class $C^\infty$ in the extension sense on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ with $\chi(\cdot,t_0)=0$, $\partial_t\chi(\cdot,t_0)=0$ and $W\chi=G$ on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$; the transformed pair $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$, has the same field pair $(E,B)$, and any two such gauge functions differ by a solution of $W\chi=0$. This is the exact content of [[lem-em-gauge-wave-reachability]] read for potential pairs of the framework; its physical content is that every smooth potential representation of a field pair on a slab admits a Lorenz-gauge representative with zero gauge Cauchy data at $t_0$, without changing the fields. (b) [Bounded smooth domain; Coulomb gauge] Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]), let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval and let $(\varphi,A)$ be of class $C^\infty$ on a neighbourhood of $\bar\Omega\times\bar I$. Fix a smooth time-independent Dirichlet datum $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$. Then there is a gauge function $\psi$, of class $C^\infty$ on a neighbourhood of $\bar\Omega\times\bar I$, with $\psi(\cdot,t)|_{\partial\Omega}=g$ for every $t\in I$, such that $$\operatorname{div}(A+\nabla\psi)(\cdot,t)=0\qquad\text{on }\Omega\text{ for every }t\in I;$$ the transformed pair $T_\psi(\varphi,A)$ is in Coulomb gauge on $\Omega\times I$ and has the same field pair $(E,B)$ ([[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]). The generator is unique among such generators with datum $g$; if $g=0$, then $\psi$ is the unique generator with zero boundary values. (c) [Residual freedom on star-shaped domains] Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and star-shaped ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]) and let $(\varphi,A)$, $(\tilde\varphi,\tilde A)$ be two potential pairs of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-interval]]) with the same field pair, both in Lorenz gauge. If I is non-open, these C2 classes and the resulting generator use the open-neighbourhood restriction convention of lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials; for the physical open laboratory interval they have their ordinary C2 meaning. If a degenerate I is used in this branch, choose the ambient C2 extensions as part of the data: the same-field and Lorenz conditions refer to these extensions on an ambient time neighbourhood before restriction, and their time jets are not determined uniquely by the restricted values alone. Then there is a gauge function $\chi$ of class $C^2$ jointly with $(\tilde\varphi,\tilde A)=T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ and $W\chi=0$ on $\Omega\times I$. (d) [Scope] Nothing is asserted about gauge functions meeting arbitrary prescribed boundary or initial restrictions: in (a) the gauge function has zero Cauchy data at $t_0$ and no spatial boundary condition or decay, and $\Omega$ is all of $\mathbb R^3$; in (b) the datum is the fixed time-independent Dirichlet datum $g$ and the Neumann variant with its own compatibility condition for every $t$ is not claimed; the older promise of a global Lorenz gauge on a bounded domain with prescribed boundary data is explicitly outside this result. The Coulomb-gauge statement concerns the spatial divergence in the chosen inertial chart, and the instantaneous appearance of the Coulomb potential is a property of the representation, not a signal: only the field pair $(E,B)$ is physical content ([[def-em-fields]]).
